overview: Holotype ROM 63823 and paratypes preserve mandibles, maxillipeds and subdivided basipods used to test a stem-mandibulate body plan.

ecology.diet: Feeding inferred from mandibles; prey not preserved
ecology.locomotion: Benthic or swimming mode inferred from appendages

evidenceSummary: Named material directly preserves the appendages; stem-mandibulate placement is a matrix result and does not make Tokummia an ancestor of living groups.

overview: More than 1,800 specimens document a bivalved mandibulate body plan with mandibles and serial appendages; pancrustacean placement remains analytical.

ecology.diet: Small-particle or prey feeding inferred from mandibles

evidenceSummary: The large museum series supports repeatable anatomy; pancrustacean placement and swimming-predator ecology remain topology and functional interpretations.

commonNameZh: 滇虫甲壳幼体发育系列
overview: Phosphatized individuals from several growth stages preserve exites and eucrustacean-like limb organization without fixing a crown-origin date.

ecology.habitat: Marine setting represented by Orsten-type preservation
ecology.locomotion: Limb-based swimming or crawling inferred; performance unknown

evidenceSummary: Developmental stages directly document appendage construction; crown-eucrustacean placement and epipodite homology remain character interpretations.

commonName: Contested Late Devonian arthropod (originally interpreted as an insect)
commonNameZh: 有争议的晚泥盆世节肢动物（原被解释为昆虫）
overview: The single, nearly complete Strud specimen was described as a Late Devonian insect, but a subsequent re-investigation rejected that identification; the profile preserves both the named material and the unresolved arthropod affinity.

ecology.diet: An omnivorous orthopteroid-mandible interpretation was proposed; feeding is not directly observed
ecology.habitat: Terrestrial or freshwater-margin setting inferred from the Strud sediments
ecology.locomotion: Walking arthropod inferred from preserved legs; performance is unknown

evidenceSummary: Garrouste et al. identified the specimen as an insect, whereas Hörnschemeyer et al. found that interpretation untenable after re-examination; the atlas therefore treats Strudiella as a contested arthropod sample rather than a secure insect calibration.

overview: One female and two male Yixian specimens preserve a wing shoulder pad and female abdominal operculum used to identify a stem-Phasmatodea insect, with dark wing venation interpreted as a possible leaf-mimicry signal.

ecology.diet: Plant association and leaf mimicry suggest a phytophagous context; feeding is not directly observed
ecology.habitat: Early Cretaceous terrestrial Jehol biota setting
ecology.locomotion: Winged insect with long forewings; flight capability is inferred from wing anatomy
ecology.bodySize: Approximately 47–56 mm in the described specimens (female ~56 mm; males ~47–51 mm)
ecology.guild: Putative plant-associated crypsis guild inferred from wing coloration

evidenceSummary: The primary description directly documents three Yixian specimens and the diagnostic structures used for a stem-Phasmatodea assignment; the proposed leaf mimicry remains a functional interpretation of preserved wing coloration.
